title: Development and Validation of an LC–MS/MS Method for Quantification of p-Aminohippuric Acid in Cell Lysates: Application to OAT1 Transport Studies
content: Quantification of p-aminohippuric acid (PAH) in cell lysates can support in vitro studies of organic anion transporter 1 (OAT1). This study developed a hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (HILIC–MS/MS) method for measuring PAH in lysates of human embryonic kidney cells. Samples were prepared by protein precipitation with methanol–acetonitrile, and anastrozole was used as the internal standard. The calibration range was 0.1–100.0 ng/mL, with a lower limit of quantification of 0.1 ng/mL. Selectivity, accuracy, precision, recovery, matrix effects, carryover, and stability were evaluated. The method was applied to a pilot comparison of PAH accumulation in parental HEK293 cells and HEK293-OAT1 cells expressing OAT1. PAH accumulation was higher in OAT1-expressing cells, and uptake was reduced in the presence of probenecid. These findings support the use of the assay to measure cell-associated PAH in an in vitro OAT1 model.
